meta.note: Offers are snapshots. Eligibility, limits, data terms, and availability can change at any time. Confirm on the official page before adding a payment method.

programs.name: Gemini Developer API
programs.headline: A real free tier, with a data trade-off.
programs.whatYouGet: Rate-limited access to selected Gemini models through Google AI Studio. Limits are shown per project, and an API key is available without a card.
programs.watchOut: Free-tier content may be used to improve Google products. Some models are paid-only. Do not send private, client, student, or patient data.
programs.eligibility: Google account in an eligible region. No card needed for the free tier at check.

programs.name: Groq API
programs.headline: Fast hosted models with a genuine free tier.
programs.whatYouGet: Free access to hosted open models, with limits that vary by model and apply per organization. No credit card was required at check.
programs.watchOut: Rate limits are not a monthly budget. Model availability and data terms can change; check the current limits page for the model you plan to use.
programs.eligibility: Groq account. No card at check.

programs.name: OpenRouter free models
programs.headline: One API for comparing many free model variants.
programs.whatYouGet: Free model variants from multiple providers. At check, accounts with under $10 in lifetime purchases could make 50 free-model requests per day; accounts with $10 or more could make 1,000 per day.
programs.watchOut: The free catalog rotates and provider data policies vary by model. Extra accounts do not increase shared limits. Read each model's data policy.
programs.eligibility: OpenRouter account; free variants available without a card.

programs.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
programs.headline: Small edge AI features with a daily free allowance.
programs.whatYouGet: 10,000 Neurons per day on the Workers Free plan at check, with an OpenAI-compatible API and hosted open models. Good for small app features and experiments.
programs.watchOut: Not a bulk-generation allowance. Per-model neuron costs vary, and the free plan is shared infrastructure with no production SLA. Add app-level request caps.
programs.eligibility: Cloudflare account on the Workers Free plan.

programs.name: Mistral Free mode
programs.headline: Rate-limited access to Mistral models without a card.
programs.whatYouGet: A free mode for La Plateforme with monthly usage and rate limits. Useful for testing prompts and comparing models before paying.
programs.watchOut: Mistral's documentation says free-mode data may be used for training unless you opt out. Limits live in the admin console and can change.
programs.eligibility: Mistral account. No card at check.

programs.name: Cohere trial key
programs.headline: Evaluation access to Cohere models.
programs.whatYouGet: A free trial API key for evaluation, rate-limited and limited to a monthly call quota. Useful for a quick proof of concept.
programs.watchOut: Trial keys are for evaluation, not production. The exact quota and model access can change; confirm in the dashboard before relying on it.
programs.eligibility: Cohere account. No card for a trial key.

programs.name: NVIDIA NIM hosted APIs
programs.headline: Developer access to hosted NVIDIA model endpoints.
programs.whatYouGet: Free developer access to hosted NIM endpoints, including OpenAI-compatible APIs and a starting credit allotment. You can request more credits from the developer account.
programs.watchOut: Intended for development and evaluation, not production scale. Credits, model access, and throughput can change.
programs.eligibility: NVIDIA Developer Program account.

programs.name: AWS Free Tier
programs.headline: A credit-based six-month free plan, not the old 12-month story.
programs.whatYouGet: New accounts get $100 in credits and can earn up to another $100 through activities. The Free account plan lasts up to six months and includes always-free allowances; some services are excluded.
programs.watchOut: Older guides describe a twelve-month everything-free tier. The Free account plan does not charge until you upgrade, but the account closes at the end if unused. Paid plan usage beyond credits is billed.
programs.eligibility: New AWS customer; company and billing details required. A payment method is generally part of signup.

programs.name: Google Cloud Free
programs.headline: A generous 90-day lab with narrow always-free limits.
programs.whatYouGet: $300 in welcome credit for 90 days, plus Always Free services including an e2-micro VM in specific U.S. regions, 5 GB of Cloud Storage, and limited BigQuery usage.
programs.watchOut: Always Free is region- and service-specific. Budget alerts do not cap spending. After the trial, services can stop until you upgrade.
programs.eligibility: Google Cloud billing account with a credit card.

programs.name: Azure free account
programs.headline: $200 for 30 days, plus a year of selected free services.
programs.whatYouGet: $200 credit for 30 days and free quantities of selected Azure services for 12 months.
programs.watchOut: A card is required for verification, and the account is disabled if you do not move to pay-as-you-go after the credit expires or the 30 days end. Azure budgets alert but do not stop resources.
programs.eligibility: New Azure customer; card verification.

programs.name: Oracle Cloud Free Tier
programs.headline: An always-free VM tier, subject to capacity and reclamation.
programs.whatYouGet: $300 trial credit plus Always Free resources: two AMD micro VMs, an A1 allowance equivalent to 2 OCPUs and 12 GB running continuously at check, and two small Autonomous Databases.
programs.watchOut: Idle compute can be reclaimed. Popular shapes and home-region capacity are limited. The A1 allowance is lower than older guides claim, and object storage above 20 GB can be deleted at trial end.
programs.eligibility: Oracle Cloud account; card verification is generally required.

programs.name: Vercel Hobby
programs.headline: Free and polished, but not for commercial use.
programs.whatYouGet: A free personal plan with monthly CDN, data, and function allowances. Overages were hard-capped at check rather than billed.
programs.watchOut: Hobby is for personal, non-commercial use. A business site for an LLC should use a plan that permits commercial use.
programs.eligibility: Personal projects only; not commercial use.

programs.name: Render Free
programs.headline: Small apps and demos that can sleep.
programs.whatYouGet: Free web services with limited RAM, fractional CPU, and monthly bandwidth. Services sleep after inactivity, and no card was required for the free plan at check.
programs.watchOut: Cold starts and sleeping services are not a production experience. Resource limits and availability can change.
programs.eligibility: Anyone; free plan.

programs.name: GitHub Pages
programs.headline: Free static hosting for public repositories.
programs.whatYouGet: Host static HTML, CSS, JavaScript, documentation, and small tools from a public repository, with HTTPS and custom domains.
programs.watchOut: No server-side code. Usage and acceptable-use limits apply, and the repository is public. Do not publish secrets or private data.
programs.eligibility: GitHub account and a public repository.

programs.name: Hugging Face Spaces
programs.headline: Free CPU demos for open models.
programs.whatYouGet: Free CPU-hosted Spaces with usage limits. GPU upgrades and higher hardware are paid.
programs.watchOut: Free compute is limited and can sleep. Free accounts do not include Inference Providers credits. Check visibility, data policies, and hardware limits.
programs.eligibility: Hugging Face account.

programs.name: Google Colab
programs.headline: Free notebook compute, when it is available.
programs.whatYouGet: Hosted notebooks with variable free GPU and TPU access. Good for learning, one-off experiments, and public tutorials.
programs.watchOut: Free GPU access is not guaranteed, sessions expire, and the environment is not production hosting. Do not process sensitive data.
programs.eligibility: Google account; free tier.

programs.name: Kaggle Notebooks
programs.headline: Free notebooks, datasets, and limited accelerators.
programs.whatYouGet: A hosted notebook environment with limited weekly GPU and TPU quotas, plus public datasets for learning.
programs.watchOut: Quotas, session limits, and verification requirements vary. Do not upload private data, and do not treat a free notebook as production infrastructure.
programs.eligibility: Kaggle account; phone verification may be required for accelerators.

programs.name: AWS Activate
programs.headline: A useful base tier, with larger numbers gated by stage.
programs.whatYouGet: Activate Founders offers around $1,000 in credits at check, with select startups eligible for up to $5,000 over time. Portfolio tier through Activate Providers advertises up to $200,000 for qualifying startups.
programs.watchOut: Higher tiers require provider affiliation, stage, and usage criteria. Credits expire and may exclude some services. This is not a free-API allowance.
programs.eligibility: Real company, website, and AWS account; higher tiers require an Activate Provider or investor relationship.

programs.name: Google for Startups Cloud
programs.headline: From a $2,000 pre-funded tier to large AI-first credits.
programs.whatYouGet: Up to $2,000 for pre-funded startups, up to $200,000 for eligible funded startups, and up to $350,000 for AI-first startups over two years at check.
programs.watchOut: Higher tiers require evidence, funding or an AI-first qualification. Read credit eligibility and expiry terms before building around the headline number.
programs.eligibility: Eligible startup with a product and website; tier-specific funding and accelerator requirements.

programs.name: Microsoft for Startups
programs.headline: A small starting credit with a path to more.
programs.whatYouGet: Up to $200 in Azure credits immediately, with the ability to unlock up to $150,000 over time for qualifying startups through verification and program milestones.
programs.watchOut: The upper tiers are not automatic. LinkedIn and business verification are required, and this is separate from the Azure free account.
programs.eligibility: For-profit, privately held software startup; verification and stage criteria.

programs.name: Claude for Startups
programs.headline: Closed at check; plan around the cohort, not the headline.
programs.whatYouGet: At check, the public cohort was full and not accepting new applications. The program advertises partner offers and API credits for eligible startups; additional credits can be available through partner VCs.
programs.watchOut: This is not a self-serve sign-up bonus. Availability changes and credits may be tied to a partner relationship. Do not put it in a budget you need this month.
programs.eligibility: Cohort and partner criteria; public applications were closed at check.

programs.name: OpenAI for Startups
programs.headline: A partner-VC route, not a general signup credit.
programs.whatYouGet: API credits, higher rate limits, and technical support for eligible startups, generally through partner venture capital firms.
programs.watchOut: A partner referral code is required. Credit amounts are not a public self-serve offer, and individual accounts do not receive routine free API credits.
programs.eligibility: Startup backed by a partner VC; application and org details.

programs.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack
programs.headline: The best developer bundle, if you are genuinely enrolled.
programs.whatYouGet: Verified students can access a changing bundle that includes Copilot Student, Codespaces allowances, Azure for Students credit, JetBrains educational licenses, and domain offers.
programs.watchOut: Each benefit has its own limits and expiry. Education benefits are for learning and generally not a license for commercial work. Re-verification may be required.
programs.eligibility: Verified student; school email or enrollment documentation.

programs.name: Gemini for Students
programs.headline: A year of Google AI, not free API credits.
programs.whatYouGet: At check, up to 12 months of Google AI Pro for eligible U.S. college students age 18+, or Google AI Plus in 140+ other markets.
programs.watchOut: This is a consumer plan, not a Gemini API credit. Check whether a card or auto-renewal is required, and set a reminder before the offer ends.
programs.eligibility: Eligible college students; verification and regional rules apply.

programs.name: Azure for Students
programs.headline: $100 in Azure credit without a credit card.
programs.whatYouGet: $100 in Azure credit for 12 months, plus free monthly amounts of selected services. No credit card was required at check.
programs.watchOut: For student educational use, with annual renewal and service exclusions. It is not a business account and does not remove the need to monitor resources.
programs.eligibility: Full-time university student with academic verification.

programs.name: Google for Nonprofits
programs.headline: Google tools and Ad Grants for eligible charities.
programs.whatYouGet: Access to no-cost and discounted Google tools for eligible nonprofits, plus programs such as Google Ad Grants, which offers up to $10,000 per month in search advertising.
programs.watchOut: In the U.S., eligibility generally requires 501(c)(3) charitable status and validation. Ad Grants is advertising credit, not AI API credit. An LLC is not eligible.
programs.eligibility: Registered charitable organization in an eligible country; validation required.

programs.name: Microsoft for Nonprofits
programs.headline: Cloud grants and discounts for validated nonprofits.
programs.whatYouGet: Grants and discounts across Microsoft cloud solutions including Azure, Microsoft 365, and Dynamics, subject to eligibility.
programs.watchOut: Validation is required, not every product is included, and one grant tenant per organization may apply. An LLC is not eligible.
programs.eligibility: Eligible nonprofit validated through Microsoft's nonprofit process.

programs.name: AWS Nonprofit Credit Program
programs.headline: Promotional credits for eligible nonprofits.
programs.whatYouGet: AWS promotional credits for eligible nonprofits; AWS's public nonprofit pages advertised amounts up to $5,000 depending on the program and path at check.
programs.watchOut: Validation and annual limits apply, eligible services vary, and the separate AWS Imagine Grant has its own process. Do not assume credits cover third-party or support costs.
programs.eligibility: Eligible nonprofit; AWS and TechSoup validation.

programs.name: TechSoup
programs.headline: The validation hub behind many nonprofit offers.
programs.whatYouGet: Validation and access to donated or discounted software and services from many vendors.
programs.watchOut: An administrative fee may apply, each vendor has separate eligibility rules, and validation can take time. A for-profit LLC is not eligible.
programs.eligibility: Nonprofits, charities, libraries, and some public agencies, depending on the vendor.

programs.name: Ollama
programs.headline: Run models locally with no per-token meter.
programs.whatYouGet: A free open-source runner for local language models, with a simple CLI and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Supports CPU and GPU acceleration where available.
programs.watchOut: You pay for hardware and electricity. Small models may not match hosted frontier models. Model licenses vary, and local is not automatically secure.
programs.eligibility: Your own computer; no account required.

programs.name: Open WebUI
programs.headline: A self-hosted chat front end for local models.
programs.whatYouGet: A free, self-hosted chat interface for local or remote model servers, with multi-user and document features.
programs.watchOut: Check the current license and secure authentication before exposing it. You own maintenance, updates, and backups.
programs.eligibility: Self-hosted on your own machine or server.

programs.name: Aider
programs.headline: Open-source pair programming in the terminal.
programs.whatYouGet: An open-source AI pair programmer that edits files in a Git repository and supports hosted or local models.
programs.watchOut: It can change and commit files. Review diffs, work on a branch, and back up. Output quality depends on the model you connect.
programs.eligibility: Your machine; model provider optional.

programs.name: Continue
programs.headline: An open-source coding assistant for your IDE.
programs.whatYouGet: A free IDE extension for chat and code assistance that can connect to local or hosted models.
programs.watchOut: Model costs or hardware costs are separate. Review extension permissions and suggestions; code generation is not a substitute for tests.
programs.eligibility: Your machine with a supported IDE.

programs.name: ComfyUI
programs.headline: Node-based local image generation.
programs.whatYouGet: An open-source interface for Stable Diffusion and related image pipelines, running locally with no per-image API bill.
programs.watchOut: Needs a capable GPU for comfortable use. Model licenses and content policies apply, setup is technical, and you own the safety checks.
programs.eligibility: Your own hardware.

programs.name: Whisper
programs.headline: Local speech-to-text without an API bill.
programs.whatYouGet: Open-source speech recognition models that run on CPU or GPU, available through the command line and many local apps.
programs.watchOut: Accuracy varies by audio and language. Do not transcribe patient, student, or client audio without consent and a compliance plan. Larger models need more resources.
programs.eligibility: Your own hardware.

programs.name: n8n community edition
programs.headline: Self-hosted automation with local AI hooks.
programs.whatYouGet: A fair-code workflow automation platform with a free community edition you can self-host and connect to local models and services.
programs.watchOut: It is not OSI open source; the Sustainable Use License restricts hosting and resale. Secure it, back it up, and review the license before building a business on it.
programs.eligibility: Self-hosted; license terms apply.
